narrative:
The model determined that you have a 68% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is well above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were your credit history, the status of your checking account, and the purpose of the loan. Your credit history showed that all previous credits at this bank have been paid, which is relatively uncommon. Among approved applicants this category appears in only about 3% of cases, and unfortunately the model interpreted this specific pattern as increasing your risk. The status of your checking account (currently between 0 and 200 DM) also pushed the prediction toward denial; most approved applicants either have no checking account or hold substantially higher balances. Finally, the fact that the loan is intended for a new car added further weight toward a bad-credit outcome, as new-car purchases are associated with higher risk in the data the model has learned from.

Taken together, these three pieces of information outweighed several positive signals such as your modest loan amount, steady employment, and low installment rate relative to income.

You should focus on improving the areas the model weighed most heavily. Building a longer track record of on-time payments, increasing your checking-account balance, and perhaps reconsidering the loan purpose or amount could improve your prospects next time. Consider re-applying in six to twelve months after making visible progress on these points.
